newsitem.title: GERMANY: DTB Bunds hit by profit taking, but seen recoverin.
newsitem.headline: DTB Bunds hit by profit taking, but seen recoverin.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were hit by profit-taking in late session trade on Tuesday as investors cashed in on a recent strong rally in the market.

While prices were substantially lower than Monday's closing levels, analysts said that since the market had only given back some of the previous session's gains, the outlook remained relatively positive.

Major support for the September DTB contract in the 102.54 to 102.60 area, while breached earlier when the future dipped to 102.58, should hold at the close, analysts said, suggesting more gains will be clocked up later in the week.
"The market ran up ealier in the session, partly on the back of the unemployment figures," said Charles Diebel, senior fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London.
But he said that with the unmeployment data "not conclusively bullish" the rally petered out and profit-takers were prompted to step in and book their gains.

Unemployment in Germany rose to a seasonally-adjusted 4.37 million in June, an increase of 11,000 from the previous month. But in percentage terms, the seasonally-adjusted rate remained steady at 11.4 percent.
September DTB Bund futures, which racheted up to test the contract high at 102.92 in earlier business, were 18 basis points lower on the day at 103.65 by 1416 GMT.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was quoted at 103.15 for a bid yield of 5.572 percent by the same time, with the yield spread to 10-year Treasuries broadly steady at 81 basis points.
Analysts said that with little in the way of major economic data coming up, the market was likely to take stock from this session's consolidative downmove and head higher in the next few sessions.
"The sentiment is still fairly positive here," said a Frankfurt-based trader. "I don't see anything coming up that should stop people from continuing to follow this uptrend."

On the technical side, analysts said the main upside target for the September contract was at 103.00, but said any rally would have to be strongh enough to push through an intervening barrier at 102.92 -- the currenct contract high.
"This session's downmove is corrective in nature," said one. "As long as 102.43 (support) is firm, buying dips up to 103.00 is still favoured."
